title: Post-discharge clinical course following microbiological culture collection in the emergency department
summary:
Many patients who come to the emergency department with a suspected infection are discharged home after initial tests and treatment. In these cases, laboratory tests to detect bacteria or other pathogens—especially in blood or urine—are sometimes questioned, because their benefit is not always clear and the results do not always influence treatment decisions.

At the same time, it is known that antibiotic treatment tailored to the results of such microbiological tests can lead to better outcomes, reduce the development of antibiotic resistance, and improve treatment safety.

While there are well-established procedures for using these tests in patients who are admitted to the hospital, it is still unclear how useful they are for patients who are treated in the emergency department and then sent home, and whether the results lead to changes in treatment.

The aim of the PostCult study is to systematically collect information on microbiological tests (such as blood and urine tests) performed in patients with suspected infections who are discharged from the emergency departments of Virchow Klinikum and Charité Campus Mitte. In addition, patients will be contacted by phone after discharge to understand how their treatment continued and how their condition developed.
conditions: Microbiological testing (blood and urine cultures) in patients discharged from the emergency department

interventions.name: This is a prospective cohort study with a 7-day follow-up period. Patients who have had a blood or urine culture taken as part of their routine care in the emergency department and are subsequently discharged home will be included. Participation in the study does not involve any additional procedure

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age ≥ 18 years
-Collection of a blood or urine culture during the emergency department visit
-Outpatient management (discharge from the emergency department)
-Ability to provide informed consent
-Availability for follow-up (telephone contact available)
Exclusion criteria:
Language barrier
